scope: Proposition 6.9 (Sharp-island geometric contract) of the manuscript “Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2” (preprints/Strong-diffeomorphic-approximation-in-three-dimensions-for-p-gt-2-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 368 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 824a96588feb42d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 97. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix η, the compact chart and basis bounds, and the finite template choices above. The calibrated islands admit pre-stacks with all the qualitative properties of Definition 4.2 and with the following quantitative properties. 1. Throughout an enlarged equal-weight island the pre-slope density is at most CMσ in aligned units. This constant is independent of microscopic master widths, central crossing angles, final guard gaps, H, W, and the final level-count tolerance δ′. 2. In deep regular low-leakage portions, the scalar gradients obey (6.6). At concurrent independent strips the two-coordinate squared Frobenius cost is at most 2 + Cη. At an occupied diagonal transition after routing, the active coordinate has gradient ±∇uj ± ∇uk, whose squared norm has the same bound. In parallel mode the opponent bands are disjoint in these portions and the squared norm is at most 1 + Cη. Occupied-stair speeds multiply these bounds by at most (1 + Cζ)2. 3. In a regular tetrahedron the excluded CNW neighborhoods of its faces, all its main slab creases, and its non-slab disks occupy relative volume at most CN  W H + δ′  . (6.9) The canonical protection and broadening margins only change the fixed factor CN . Nonregular tetrahedra, high-leakage tetrahedra, their required fixed-neighbor layers, and patch boundary margins are charged by their full Mp-cost. The norm statements concern the smooth compatible label sectors after the combined label barrier, away from central radial activation cutoffs. They are geometric scalar-pair estimates; their physical conversion and the saturation argument are made in Lemma 7.6.
